chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hands of two men, so one of them divorced and the other refused. So Ali (peace be upon him) refused to validate that until they both gather upon the divorce together.
And it is reported that he (peace be upon him) did not allow the representation in the divorce.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce when delegated to two agents who disagree?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the mechanics of *wakalah* (agency) in divorce, establishing that delegated authority requires joint consensus; if one agent acts while the other refuses, the divorce is invalid. It further reports a broader view that general representation in divorce may be impermissible, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the husband's direct intent (*niyyah*) in dissolving the marital bond. This ruling underscores the legal precision required in family law to prevent unilateral or ambiguous dissolution of marriage.
